source.title: The Role of Information Complexity and Randomization in Representation Learning
source.authors: Matías Vera; Pablo Piantanida; L. Vega

record.tranche_reason: The study measures training–test generalization gaps and how they change with network size, dropout, and label mismatch, using information complexity as a related measure. These findings do not measure the specific outcomes named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on gap and information complexity. Its random- and roll-label experiment measures gap during retraining, not held-out accuracy or whether a network memorizes random labels. The cited results of other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures an absolute cross-entropy generalization gap and an information-complexity surrogate, neither of which establishes the outcomes in V1–V8. Increasing gaps do not establish increasing test error, and reducing gaps with dropout does not establish lower held-out classification error. Its theoretical dropout result concerns a risk surrogate.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report an apparent association between information complexity and generalization gap across width, noise, and label mismatch. Their broader conclusion advocates invariant representations and noise based on an information-theoretic gap bound and a risk-surrogate analysis. They acknowledge that mathematical guarantees for mismatch detection remain open.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures gap and an information-complexity surrogate in dropout networks; it does not use the interventions or measures specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured gap varies with network size and dropout rate; the CIFAR-10 gap is described as more sensitive to dropout rate than the MNIST gap. Label mismatch also changes the gap and information-complexity trajectory.

fits_no_version.finding: Across tested widths, the absolute cross-entropy generalization gap and square-root information-complexity surrogate tend to increase together.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information complexity tracks the absolute cross-entropy gap across widths in these dropout networks trained on 5K examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing retention probability while holding expected active units constant changes the gap and complexity surrogate similarly; the CIFAR-10 gap is more sensitive than the MNIST gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The information-complexity surrogate tracks gap changes across noise and architecture choices in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Separate transitions from normal-label training to roll-label or random-label training alter gap and complexity trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information complexity can indicate training-label distribution changes in sequential training, without establishing random-label memorization accuracy.

record.problems: The plotted experimental values are not stated numerically in the text. The authors average five repetitions but report no uncertainty interval here. The experiments use 5K training samples and dropout networks; the label-mismatch experiment's stated assumptions do not apply to the roll- or random-label phases.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported outcomes beyond the six rows were identified. Exact curve values are figure-only and were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting and above-chance natural-label accuracy under the same recipe, with chance held-out random-label accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out classification error, including small-data, excessive-dropout, and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites original sources for V1, V2, and V6 but supplies no direct test of those versions. All six rows concern related constructs, so their partial states should become cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. The label-mismatch phases violate the shared-distribution assumption of the study's gap theorem.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy or report random-label fit.
Reports gap across network sizes, but not whether test error keeps falling after zero training error or the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Reports gap as dropout changes, but does not establish that dropout lowers test error versus no dropout or report the small-training-set and excessive-dropout regimes.
Measures information complexity, not magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove and retrain on selected memorized examples.

rows.subject: 3-layer feed-forward neural networks (MNIST)
rows.size_stated: 4 to 2048 hidden units; same number per layer
rows.stage_stated: trained with dropout; early stopping based on validation misclassification error
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of hidden units and measured generalization gap and surrogate information complexity.
rows.uncertainty: Experiments repeated five times and averaged; error bars not stated
rows.note: Text describes an increasing monotonous tendency for both curves as network size increases; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The increasing absolute cross-entropy gap does not measure V2's test-error trend beyond interpolation; zero training error is not established. The complexity plotted is a square-root surrogate derived from an upper bound. pout = 0.8 is the retention probability.

rows.subject: Feed-forward neural networks (MNIST)
rows.size_stated: m·pout = 256 for each of the first two hidden layers and 512 for the last hidden layer
rows.stage_stated: trained with dropout; early stopping based on validation misclassification error
rows.operation_detail: Varied dropout rate while holding the expected number of present units fixed, and measured gap and surrogate information complexity.
rows.uncertainty: Experiments repeated five times and averaged; error bars not stated
rows.note: Authors say noise controls generalization as pout goes down; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: A smaller absolute cross-entropy gap does not establish V6's lower held-out error. Width changes with retention probability to hold expected active units constant. Figure 2 spans pout = 0.5–1, including no dropout at 1; pout denotes retention probability.

rows.subject: Feed-forward neural network, layers 784-256-256-256-10
rows.stage_stated: trained for 90 epochs per dataset phase
rows.operation_detail: Retrained sequentially on normal labels, then roll labels, then random labels, measuring gap and surrogate information complexity over epochs.
rows.note: Text says the gap increases after transition to roll labels and reports a clear information-complexity transition relative to normal labels; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: Correct the sequence to normal labels, a second normal-label subset, then roll labels, each for 90 epochs on 5K samples. Roll and random labels are separate experiments. The mismatch gap does not establish V1's random-label fit and held-out accuracy. pout = 0.8 is retention probability.
